newsitem.title: CANADA: Arakis climbs as CEO meets with investors.
newsitem.headline: Arakis climbs as CEO meets with investors.

text.p: Shares of Arakis Energy Corp rose above a longtime ceiling of $4 on Wednesday as the company's chief executive met with institutional investors and speculation mounted over a possible major oil discovery.
Calgary-based Arakis, part of a consortium developing a 12.2-million-acre oil concession in Sudan, climbed 1/4 to 4-1/8 with over 2.2 million shares changing hands in early trade.
The stock had been stuck below the $4 level for months despite several developments, including the formation of the international consortium to develop the huge block.
Arakis chief executive John McLeod was meeting this week with institutional investors in New York and Boston.

McLeod has spent most of his time since mid-December making sure the deal with China National Petroleum Corp, Malysian state oil company Petronas and the Sudan government was finalized, said Kirk Dornbush, president of Atlanta-based Diem Investments. The firm holds Arakis stock in a hedge fund.

"Now that it's finalized he can spend time telling the story," Dornbush said. "All of us institutional holders are on the one hand very pleased with what he is doing operationally. But our bottom line is the bottom line."
Close observers also said speculation was mounting over the consortium's Umm Sagura well, which had reportedly reached total depth.
The well was targeting a potentially huge reservoir that Arakis geologists had dubbed "the Pink Panther."
However, Dornbush cautioned that results from well tests could still be several weeks away.
Results, meanwhile, were expected in the coming days from the group's El Toor and Toma South delineation wells and from completion tests of its El Nar discovery.
